en: One fascicle of the *Aśvaghoṣa-bodhisattva-siddhi-mantra-japa* (brought by Minister Kibi);
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Da Guangzhi of Daxingshan Temple.
Translated by Imperial Decree by [Name]:

At that time, the Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying: "I possess a great supernatural power, an extremely secret dhāraṇī, which I wish to proclaim for the sake of liberating sentient beings in the defiled worlds of the future age of dharma decay. May the Buddha grant me permission. The Buddha granted his consent.
Then the Buddha, the World-Honored One, praised the Bodhisattva, saying: "Excellent, excellent! You have the permission of all Buddhas;

all Bodhisattvas and devas likewise rejoice. You may speak with speed. Thereupon the Bodhisattva rose from his seat, joined his palms, bowed his head, and with leaping joy circumambulated the Buddha three times to the right.
He withdrew to sit at one side before the Buddha and immediately spoke this Great [Dhāraṇī].
The divine mantra is: Namo samantabuddhānām, karmavardhana hūṃ dṛk ṭrik paha.
At that time, having spoken these sublime mantras, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
the heavens rained down maṇḍala flowers, and the earth gushed forth the seven treasures.

All sentient beings attained siddhi, and wealth, cotton, brocade, gold, and jewels arose like mountains—a rarity indeed in this world. If there are those, whether householders or renunciants, who are virtuous...
If a man or a woman upholds even a single syllable of this sublime mantra and my name once passes through their ears,

the karmic retribution of extreme poverty throughout all successive lives will be swiftly extinguished; they shall quickly achieve fulfillment in all worldly and supramundane splendors and requisites for happiness,
and shall make offerings to the Triple Gem, their six kin, their nine clans, and indeed to all beggars.
Grant alms and offerings so that nothing may be contrary to one's wishes.

If you wish to receive and uphold this dharma, first paint an image of the Bodhisattva with six arms, seated upon a red lotus flower and a white horse, surrounded by the six great messengers. Once the painting is completed, receive the transmission from the master.
One should offer to the Master the mantras, fine silks, clean garments, and even one's wife, children, kinsmen, and all possessed wealth and treasures;
I shall then rejoice and bestow the grace of all jewels. If one makes such a vow, it must not be heard by those who lack faith, nor may it be spoken to them.
Even if they were to receive, study, and practice the Way, no spiritual response would be attained.

The value of this wondrous mantra is equal to the merit of countless Buddhas. If one develops faith and makes offerings with reverence to the practitioner of yoga, honoring them as one would a Buddha, then those who receive and uphold these wondrous phrases shall obtain great merit as previously described.
Should there be kings, ministers, or various minor rulers whose lands and all things are withered and exhausted, and whose five grains do not flourish...
There shall be bountiful harvests and silkworms shall not fail to thrive; though silk, embroidery, wealth, and cotton may be scarce,
if one practices this Dharma for three months within the year— namely on the third day of the third month, the fifth day of the fifth month, and the ninth day of the ninth month—
and offers various exquisite flowers and diverse delicacies of food and drink as offerings, the five grains will flourish and ten thousand fruits will ripen in abundance throughout the land.
May all the people be fully satisfied with every kind of pleasure found among gods and humans. The dimensions of the ritual mandala should be two and a half cubits;

it should be smeared with cow dung and various famous incenses mixed with mud. At the four corners of the "Virtuous Vase" (bhadraghaṭa), one should place *vīdara* incense from the ten directions, whether burnt or unburnt.
If this incense is not used, the rite will not be accomplished. The ritual offerings provided shall be used until the devotee’s faith is established.
Without being summoned, the Bodhisattva comes of his own accord to accept their sincere offerings and fulfill the wishes of the donors.
If faithful men or women— regardless of whether they are pure or impure— daily at dawn recite this sublime mantra one hundred and eight times,
along with seven recitations of the Bodhisattva’s hymn of praise, [the Bodhisattva] will never depart from their person throughout all worldly existences.
Furthermore, it reveals the retribution of one's past deeds and brings about the fulfillment of official rank, merit, longevity, and all wishes.
Moreover, regarding the mudrā: interlace the ten fingers with the right hand over the left, keeping the wrists separated; seal the five locations with this mudrā.
By the power of binding the mudrā and reciting the mantra, immeasurable karmic retributions, curses, incantations, and malevolent spirits are extinguished.

The poisonous harms of the spirits and *chi-mei* demons of this world, and all calamities, shall be averted; one shall obtain immeasurable merit, experience immeasurable happiness in the present life, and in the future life, be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The details and sequence can be seen therein; furthermore, one may receive and practice the ritual manuals (*fusho*) and the arts of great spiritual efficacy and rapid response.
Once collated, there are texts from the Kōwa, Ten’nin, Ōtei, and Hōen eras; however, some characters are damaged by bookworms.
Because it is clear, I have omitted [redundant details].
Completed copying from the manuscript preserved at Kōzan-ji on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of the *katsuzi* year of the Bunpō era. First proofread by Jishun.
